cruise.label: Cruise line
cruise.headline: Plan the whole voyage
cruise.body: Shape the itinerary, then keep each call’s requests and confirmations in view.

agent.label: Port agent
agent.headline: Keep the call in view
agent.body: Bring service requests, decisions and readiness together around each port call.

dmc.label: DMC / shorex
dmc.headline: Keep shore plans together
dmc.body: Follow shore requests through quotes and bookings, with the call as their context.

operator.label: Tour operator
operator.headline: Keep departures ready
operator.body: Bring bookings, capacity and guide preparation into view.

platform.label: Plan
platform.title: A voyage starts years ahead
platform.body: Aster Brisa is assigned to a proposed summer voyage. The itinerary is still a draft.

platform.label: Review
platform.title: Review before publication
platform.body: Marine operations, shorex and commercial review are distinct from confirming a port call.

platform.label: Request
platform.title: Request a shore quote
platform.body: A shore request belongs to this call and names the DMC. A pending request is not a confirmed booking.

platform.label: Confirm
platform.title: Accept the returned quote
platform.body: After the DMC returns a valid quote, the cruise line can accept it into a booking. This example stops at that commitment.

embark.label: Departure
embark.title: Prepare the departure
embark.body: An independent kayaking operator prepares a departure for direct guests. Platform is not required.

embark.label: Change
embark.title: A smaller capacity changes the picture
embark.body: The example now has ten available seats for twelve booked guests. The shortfall stays visible.

embark.label: Review
embark.title: Review the available options
embark.body: The responsible person reviews capacity and guest arrangements. The example does not choose for them.
